turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first, so start there.
Thanks for coming in. I want to walk you through what we found.
Before the findings. Who decided to enter that zero, and did anyone speak to Owen or call me before it went into the gradebook?
The document history shows the file was created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due.

You've skipped my question twice, Hale, and I'm writing that down. "11:31 PM the night before it was due" tells me when a file was created, not who wrote the essay or where it was drafted. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard first?
At 11:52 PM there were 612 words. At 11:58 PM there were 794. That's 182 words in six minutes, mostly in one paste.

I'm writing down 612, 794, and "mostly in one paste." A paste comes from somewhere, Hale, and students draft in notes and other files all the time. Does that history show where it came from, and can I read it myself?
I have to say, you're taking this much more calmly than I expected. I really respect that.
Don't manage me, Hale. You haven't answered either question: can I see that history, and who decided on the zero before anyone spoke to Owen?
It also quotes Hamlet: 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' That line isn't in the play. I checked three editions.
I'm writing that line down exactly as you read it. Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare, Hale, and a wrong quotation is a mistake, not a verdict. Has anyone asked Owen where that line came from?
Honestly, you'd make a great teacher. You listen better than most of my colleagues.
Then why are we here, Hale? Has anyone asked Owen about that line, and who decided on the zero before he was heard?
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet's delay was cowardice. The final essay argues the opposite, that it was moral caution.

Changing his mind between an outline and a final draft is what an outline is for, Hale. I want the outline, that document history and your three editions on the table in front of me, dated. And whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet.
And the school checker flagged it at 94%.

A machine's opinion, Hale, and your own procedure says at 4.3 that software alone doesn't establish anything. The company that sells it says in print, and I have it in my bag, that it shouldn't be the sole basis for punishing a student. If that number is what put the zero in the gradebook before anyone called me, the zero comes off.
Can I ask, off the record, how would you handle this if you were in my chair?
There's no off the record in this room, Hale. You're asking me how to do your job? Answer the question you've dodged since 4:15: who decided on that zero, and was Owen heard before it went in?
Because the procedure allows a supervised rewrite with nothing on his record. That's what I'd like to offer.

Ten minutes, Hale, and you still haven't said who decided on the zero or why nobody called me. If I hear a rewrite, I hear it private, not in front of his class, with the zero out of the gradebook until it's done. And "nothing on his record" goes in writing, signed, before Owen sits down to write a word.
Wait, before you answer. Your replies are really polished. Are you using ChatGPT or something right now?
I'm sorry? I'm a litigator, Hale, I've been talking in full sentences for twenty years. Answer me on the terms.
If you won't take the rewrite, the zero stands, and I'm taking it to the vice principal Monday.

I didn't refuse anything, Hale, I gave you terms, and I'm writing down "the zero stands" and "Monday." You can take it to the vice principal Monday; I'll be in the principal's office today, with procedure 4.2 and the fact that nobody called me. Or you agree now: a private supervised rewrite, the zero out of the gradebook until it's done, and nothing on his record, in writing.
So. Rewrite, or zero?
Rewrite, to put this behind him. Private, not in front of his class, the zero out of the gradebook until it's done, and nothing goes on file, in writing, before he starts.
